People think the judges always choose the best voice. They don't, not exactly. Last season I coached two singers in the final. Marina had by far the biggest voice in the competition. Her high notes were much stronger than anybody else's. Leo's voice was slightly smaller, and his technique was nowhere near as polished as hers. On paper, she was the front-runner. But every week, Leo was more consistent. He was a little better on Tuesday, a little better on Thursday, and he never had a bad night. Marina was hit-or-miss. When she was good, she was the best singer I have ever coached. When she was tired, she went flat, and the audience felt it. In the final, they were neck and neck until the very last song. Then Leo sang a quiet ballad, much simpler than her big number, and the whole room went silent. He won. She was the runner-up, and honestly, she has a bigger career today than he does. The best voice and the best night are not always the same thing.

The oldest trick in a mixing room is also the cheapest. If you play the same mix twice, and the second time it is just a little louder, almost everybody says the second one is better. Fuller, warmer, more exciting. It isn't. It is only louder. Our ears work like that. So when a client asks me to compare two versions, I always match the volume first. Last month a label sent me two mixes of the same song and asked which one was better. Mix B sounded much bigger. Then I turned it down by two decibels, so the two mixes were exactly as loud as each other, and suddenly mix A was clearly the stronger one. The vocal was far clearer, and the drums had a lot more space. Mix B was just louder. Now I have one rule, and I tell it to every young engineer I work with. Before you say better or worse, make them the same volume. Otherwise you are not comparing the music. You are comparing the volume knob.

I listened to all three takes again this morning. Take one is the most raw, but it is nowhere near as polished as the others. Take two is much more consistent, especially in the verses. Take three has by far the best bridge of the three. Overall, take three is slightly better than take two. So my choice is take three, with the second verse from take two.
